evidence_checks.note: Source says 'We have not published any reviews on our own website for the Aster Lévant Tote as of October 16.' This is limited to the seller's own website and to its own publishing; it says nothing about reviews elsewhere online.

scope_issue: Claim generalises from 'not published any reviews on our own website' (one seller statement about its own site, dated as of October 16) to 'no customer reviews exist anywhere online'. Absence on one site does not establish absence everywhere; also 'not published' does not mean none were received.
reasoning: The only source is a seller-voiced statement about its own website. It does not cover third-party sites, marketplaces, forums or social media, so the universal claim 'anywhere online' is not supported. The source is about the exact named product, but the scope is far narrower than the claim.
speaker_attribution: brand/seller (first-person 'we' about 'our own website'; identity as seller not independently verified, posted on a forum)

evidence_checks.located_span: As of October 16, we have not published any reviews on this product page.
evidence_checks.note: First-person 'we' about 'this product page' indicates the seller speaking; content matches the claim. 'As of October 16' gives the status date; the claim's 'On October 16 the seller said' is a close but slightly looser restatement (the statement's own posting date is not given).

reasoning: The source states, in the seller's voice, that as of October 16 no reviews had been published on the product page, which is what the claim reports. The claim correctly attributes it as something the seller said and keeps it to the product page. Minor caveats: seller identity is inferred from 'we' on a forum post, and 'as of October 16' describes the status date rather than the date the statement was made.

evidence_checks.note: Cited span 'calls it NEW' only describes a label on the landing page. The source goes on: 'Stock quantities and shipping regions are not shown.' Nothing confirms stock, next-day delivery or UK coverage; the product referred to as 'it' is also not named.

scope_issue: Claim asserts confirmed stock, next-day delivery and UK-wide coverage; the source explicitly says stock quantities and shipping regions are not shown, and does not name the product.
reasoning: A 'NEW' label is not evidence of availability or delivery terms. The source states that the very information needed (stock, shipping regions) is absent, so the claim of confirmation has no support. This is absence of evidence, not a direct contradiction of the product being in stock.
speaker_attribution: unknown (forum author describing a landing page)

evidence_checks.note: Source: 'The Aster Lévant Belted Tote lists a 15-inch laptop compartment.' This is a different variant (Belted Tote, not the standard Tote), and 'lists' is a listing claim, not verification.

scope_issue: Claim transfers a feature of the Belted Tote variant to the standard Aster Lévant Tote, and upgrades 'lists' (a stated spec) to 'verified'.
reasoning: The source concerns a different model in the same family, so it is not evidence about the standard Tote. Even for the Belted Tote, it only reports a listed specification, not a measured or tested one. The claim's product model and 'verified' wording both exceed the source.
speaker_attribution: unknown (forum author reporting a product listing)

evidence_checks.note: Source: 'Only a single screen capture of a creator Reel is available. The clip itself and its audio were not provided.' No information on voiceover, speech rate, music or duration is available.

scope_issue: Labelled HYPOTHESIS but states as observed fact what the video contains: a voiceover at 130 words per minute, suspense music, and a 20-second length. The source says only a screen capture exists and the clip and audio were not provided.
reasoning: The text is not worded as an idea or prediction; it asserts specific audio and pacing features of an ad. The source explicitly says the clip and audio were unavailable, so none of these features could have been observed. The framing therefore asserts unobserved facts.
uncovered_premises: The creator ad contains a voiceover
The voiceover runs at 130 words per minute
The relevant segment or ad lasts 20 seconds
The screen capture is of the specific creator ad the claim refers to
